name: Oregon (statewide)

coverage.summary: Retail, hospitality and food service employers with 500 or more employees worldwide, including chains and integrated enterprises.
coverage.employees: Hourly employees whose primary duties are in retail, hospitality or food service. Salaried workers exempt from minimum wage and workers supplied by worker-leasing companies are not covered.
notes: Head count is the average number of employees per working day over 20 or more workweeks in the current or preceding calendar year (ORS 653.422(2)).

citation.quote: An employer shall provide an employee with a work schedule in writing at least 14 calendar days before the first day of the work schedule.

premiums.label: Hours added, or shift moved without losing hours, with less than 14 days' notice

citation.quote: One hour of pay at the employee's regular rate of pay, in addition to wages earned, when the employer adds more than 30 minutes of work to the employee's work shift, changes the date or start or end time of the work shift with no loss of hours, or schedules an additional work shift or on-call shift.

premiums.label: Hours cut or shift cancelled with less than 14 days' notice

citation.quote: One-half times the employee's regular rate of pay per hour for each scheduled hour that the employee does not work when the employer subtracts hours from a regular or on-call work shift, changes the date or time of a work shift resulting in a loss of work shift hours, or cancels a regular or on-call work shift.

An employer shall compensate an employee at one and one-half times the employee's regular rate of pay for the hours worked in a work shift that are less than 10 hours after the end of the previous calendar day's work shift. Consent to work the hours does not waive the premium (OAR 839-026-0040).

exceptions.label: I asked for this change
exceptions.description: The change was requested by the employee and documented in writing.

exceptions.label: Shift swap or coverage I agreed to with a coworker
exceptions.description: Employee-initiated shift swaps or coverage agreed between employees. The employer may require pre-approval.

exceptions.label: Hours cut for documented discipline
exceptions.description: Hours reduced for disciplinary reasons with just cause, documented in writing.

exceptions.label: Threats or a public official's recommendation
exceptions.description: Operations could not begin or continue because of threats to employees or property, or on the recommendation of a public official.

exceptions.label: Utility or sewer failure
exceptions.description: Operations could not begin or continue because public utilities (electricity, water or gas) or the sewer system failed.

exceptions.label: Natural disaster or similar cause
exceptions.description: Operations could not begin or continue because of a natural disaster or a similar cause outside the employer's control.

exceptions.label: Ticketed event cancelled or moved
exceptions.description: A ticketed event was cancelled or rescheduled for reasons outside the employer's control.

exceptions.label: I'm on the voluntary standby list and agreed to the hours
exceptions.description: An employee on a voluntary standby list agreed to work the additional hours (ORS 653.432).

exceptions.label: I agreed in writing to extra hours for an absence or rush
exceptions.description: Extra hours for unanticipated customer needs or an unexpected absence that the employee consented to in writing, after any standby list was contacted.

exceptions.label: Covering for a coworker's protected leave
exceptions.description: The employer had less than 14 days' notice of another employee's protected leave (or return from leave) and changed this schedule to cover it. Added by SB 1515 (2024).

otherRights.label: Good-faith estimate of your schedule when hired
Right to decline hours not on your posted schedule
Right to ask for schedule preferences without retaliation

enforcement.agency: Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries (BOLI)

notes: Notice is measured to 12:00 a.m. on the first day of the work schedule: a premium is owed for any change made after the schedule's 14-day posting deadline, whichever shift it affects.
Changes to the start or end time of 30 minutes or less owe nothing (ORS 653.455(3)(a)); Shiftowed applies this as a 31-minute threshold.
Premiums use the regular rate of pay, which includes shift differentials but not tips, bonuses or overtime premiums.
Not calling in an on-call worker also earns half-time pay; Shiftowed does not track on-call shifts yet.
